description.html: This square water dish looks like a piece of porous grey-brown stone, with pits and bumps across the whole surface. In one inside corner there is a ledge, like a small stone, that rises above the water.

That ledge has an important job. Insects such as crickets and roaches that fall into the water can climb onto it and get out instead of drowning and fouling the water. Small lizards and hatchlings also have something to hold on to if they wade in deeper than planned.
The square shape lets you push the dish into a corner of the terrarium, where it takes up the least space. The dark, neutral color suits both desert and forest setups.

A porous surface holds more dirt than a smooth one, so brushing the dish regularly is important. Change the water every day. Once a week, also clean the corner ledge, since sediment and limescale collect on it most easily.
